title: RWB-S8-E2015-APP: the deviation section of the case record view has no read operation, no published view field names, no label for a code other than X3, no published value for the deviation service level and no escalation target
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5, R7.2, R7.3 and R9; context pack S8 rwb-deviation; split plan story line RWB-S8-E2015-APP; legacy RWB-E2-015; FSD S8 Deviation handling v3 A2.2, A2.3, A2.6 and A2.9; TSD S8 Deviation handling v2 T3.1, T3.2, T4, T5.2, T5.3, T6.1 and T-A.1; Architecture v5 slides 3, 4, 8 and 13
section: Metadata (Depends on (build), Contract dependencies); Sections 1, 3, 4, 7, 8, 11, 12.1 to 12.9, 13, 14 and 16
description: (1) The Ownership Map gives rwb-deviation two write operations, POST /cases/{caseId}/deviations and PATCH /deviations/{deviationId}, and no read, while legacy RWB-E2-015 section 12 calls DeviationQuery.forCase on the case record path with a 2 s timeout and RWB-P3-E2015-CON expects a deviation view the record composes; the read is therefore declared on the service base with a gap. (2) No source publishes the field names of that deviation view beyond the seven columns the legacy section 11 names. (3) LOV-DEVIATION publishes the codes X1 to X7 without labels, and only the label of X3, Deceased customer, is printed anywhere in the sources read for this slice. (4) The deviation service level is only described as 10 working days in the Architecture v5 slide 8 note and as Set with DL22 in FSD S8 A2.1.1, so neither its value, nor the calendar it is counted on, nor the location that holds it is published, and the parameter contract of DP-06 is not in this story's pattern set. (5) R-DEV-20 keeps the deviation in DEV_WITH_OWNER on an SLA breach and no source prints the escalation target role or the codes it covers, and no source says whether an escalation task is raised in rwb-case. (6) The pattern set carries DP-03, DP-07, DP-10, DP-14, DP-15 and DP-19, whose DP table rows add six platform H dependencies, while the plan's H row for this secondary slice is empty. (7) The eleven legacy test cases carry no level, and the case half of each is RWB-P3-E2015-APP's. (8) No source prints the user text of MSG-P7-003, which the escalation failure path of this read carries.
evidence: Context pack S8 ownership rows (Tables 1 deviation, REST operations provided 2 PATCH /deviations/{deviationId} and POST /cases/{caseId}/deviations, Events EV-06 and EV-07, Jobs 0, Workflows 1 DeviationWorkflow); TSD S8 T-A.1 two endpoints and no read; TSD S8 T3.1 DF-CAS-036 to DF-CAS-045 and no label or escalation column; TSD S8 T3.2 LOV-DEVIATION as the seven bare codes and LOV-DEV-OUTCOME as RETURNED, RE_ROUTED and CASE_ENDED; TSD S8 T4 R-DEV-20 DEV_WITH_OWNER to DEV_WITH_OWNER; FSD S8 A2.1.1 target Set with DL22; Architecture v5 slide 8 note escalates if not resolved in 10 working days; legacy RWB-E2-015 sections 4, 10, 11, 12, 13 and 16 and BR5, BR9, AC2, AC7; split plan RWB-S8-E2015-APP with acs empty and H empty; RWB-P3-E2015-APP owning legacy AC1 to AC10
area: Contract; API; reference data; service level and escalation; test levels
owner_role: Solution architect, with the rwb-deviation owner, the rwb-case contract and reference-data owners, the product owner of the deviation service level, the rule-set owner of the Deviations package and the QA lead
proposed: Publish the case deviation read as a service operation with a catalogue row, or amend the Ownership Map to carry GET /cases/{caseId}/deviations; freeze the deviation view field names in RWB-P3-E2015-CON; publish LOV-DEVIATION with a label per code and LOV-DEV-OUTCOME with a label per value; publish the deviation service level, its calendar and the row that holds it; publish the escalation target and the codes R-DEV-20 covers; record the six platform contracts as template dependencies of S8 beside the H row of the secondary slice; publish a level for each legacy test case.
